findings.text: follow-on: removing the candidates-stage --focus refusal left this pre-existing test passing for the wrong reason and now dependent on a live graph. The test still asserts that run_candidates_stage(FACILITY, CandidatesStageOptions(focus=('equilibrium',))) raises a UsageError carrying '--focus' and 'item filter', but the refusal is gone: the focused id now flows to _validate_focus, which opens a real GraphClient (the stage_env fixture mocks neither the graph nor _validate_focus) and raises 'unknown SignalSource id(s): equilibrium', whose wording happens to satisfy both assertions. I confirmed the test rests on that new wording: stripping '--focus item filter' from the unknown-id message in a scratch probe fails this test (EXIT=1, stale-test-probe.log). The module docstring at lines 6-7 ('--focus is refused because the claim query takes no item filter yet') is stale in the same way. The file is outside the reviewed node's write scope; the reviewed manifest records it as its follow_on.

follow-on: the focused pending-work filter is untested. has_pending_candidate_work now takes focus_ids and run_candidate_engine threads state.focus_ids into set_has_work_fn, but the new test replaces the engine with a stub that only calls claim_sources_for_candidates, so nothing exercises the focused pending check (a run could stop early, or never stop, for a focused id set without any test noticing); the manifest-not-found and invalid-manifest branches of _resolve_focus are likewise uncovered. An added test over has_pending_candidate_work with and without focus_ids would pin the remaining surface.

The fit shortfall is that removing the stage's --focus refusal left the pre-existing tests/cli/test_discover_candidates_stage.py::test_focus_is_refused_with_a_mechanism_message and that module's docstring assert a refusal that no longer exists in the code; the reviewed manifest flags the test as a follow-on and it is outside the node's write scope, but the node's own change is what made it stale.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all four done-when behaviours and the plan's named write paths are present and named by mechanism: the claim predicate is filtered by n.id, the pending-work re-check carries the same focus so the worker stops when only focused sources remain unjudged, a YAML manifest is expanded into the same id list, and an unknown id is refused by name from _validate_focus before any claim. justifications.reuse: the change reuses claim_batch's existing status_predicate/status_params plumbing and the _domain_filter pattern, and the manifest reader it adds is a small domain-specific one (ids-or-manifest); a search of imas_codex/cli/discover found no earlier owner of a candidates focus filter. imas_codex/standard_names/sources_manifest.py already exposes load_focus_file/expand_focus_tokens, but those dispatch on a 'kind' discriminator and validate against the standard-name schemas, so they are not reusable for a SignalSource-id manifest; the three sibling section-7 focus nodes will each grow their own reader, which is the one reuse smell here.
